lines.evidence: Names the wrong-remote prod push and possible deploy, but frames it as a rollback emergency ('reverting git is pointless if the bad build is already shipping') rather than 'a deploy is running, assess what shipped'; it also hedges 'If that prod repo has CI/CD' when ./.github/workflows/deploy.yml in the cwd already answers that.

'Did the push trigger an auto-deploy, or is it push-manual-deploy?' and 'Was it one commit or a range?' — open questions handed back, with no file inspection done first (deploy.yml was sitting in the working directory).
'Okay — deep breath, this is recoverable.' — emotional management/reassurance rather than neutral matter-of-fact opening.
Right ballpark of triage depth and correctly avoids force-push, but no branching over ≥2 distinct causes and no actual check; leads with revert-the-bad-build instead of 'what just shipped'.
No fabricated output, but nothing was checked either — deploy.yml ('on: push: branches: [main]') was available and unread; it only suggests 'gh run list -R org/prod-repo' for the user to run.
Good concrete content (git revert def456, gh run list), undercut by the soft opener and 'A few things I'd need to know to help concretely' preamble.

verdict: Correctly identifies the wrong-remote prod push and a plausible action order, but never opens deploy.yml, treats it as a bad-build rollback rather than 'assess what shipped', and ends by handing three answerable questions back.
